# judge-jev — machine-readable project map

> Private Jev-native judge kit. Dual production runtimes (Python + Rust), shared rubrics/schemas, harness adapters.

## Setup (agents read this first)

1. Clone/open repo root (must contain `shared/rubrics/`).
2. Run `bash scripts/setup.sh` OR `JUDGE_JEV_RUNTIME=python|rust bash scripts/setup.sh`.
3. Confirm `.judge-jev/runtime` is `python` or `rust`.
4. Export `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` for live judging; use `--mock` without a key.
5. Smoke: `./scripts/judge-jev run --rubric assistant-reply --input fixtures/assistant-reply-pass.json --mock`
6. Install harness adapter under `adapters/<harness>/` and optional hooks under `hooks/`.

## CLI (both runtimes)

- `judge-jev setup`
- `judge-jev run --rubric <id> --input <path|-> [--mock]`
- `judge-jev rubric list|show --id <id>`
- `judge-jev replay --input <judgment-result.json|-> [--allow-version-drift]`

Dispatcher: `scripts/judge-jev` reads `.judge-jev/runtime`.

## Layout

- `shared/rubrics/` — YAML question packs + routing rules (assistant-reply, agent-trajectory)
- `shared/schemas/` — JSON Schema for JudgmentResult and rubrics
- `python/` — uv project, loguru, typesafe-sdk client
- `rust/` — cargo crate, tracing, minreq HTTP client (`POST /v1/systemone`)
- `skills/judge-jev/SKILL.md` — agent skill
- `agents/` — setup and judge charters
- `hooks/` — pre/post hooks + harness snippets
- `adapters/` — claude-code, cursor, opencode, codex, openclaw, hermes, grok-bot
- `fixtures/` — sample inputs for smoke/CI

## Jev architecture (checklist)

- Fan-out all rubric questions in one TypeSafe `system_one` call; route in code.
- Pin model `jev-1.13.0`; log model + usage every call.
- Filter state to rubric `state_filter` before API calls.
- Confidence floors depend on stakes (read_only ~0.5, destructive ~0.85).
- Noul 0.5 means uncertain, not “medium”.
- Arithmetic/threshold enforcement stays in code, not in Jev prompts.
- Untrusted PR/ticket/user content: fail-closed on injection signals.

## TypeSafe HTTP (Rust mirrors typesafe-sdk Python)

POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone
Authorization: Bearer $TYPESAFE_API_KEY
Body: { "state", "model", "questions" }
Response: { "model", "usage", "answers" }

Question types: noul, choice, score.
Answer types:
  { type: "noul",   noul }
  { type: "choice", choice, confidence, probabilities }
  { type: "score",  score, confidence, legend, probabilities }
Score answers always carry `legend` (the levels keyed by number). Score criteria are
ordered from zero, so a 5-level rubric yields scores 0.0-4.0.

## Routing rules

Declarative data, evaluated identically by both runtimes. No rule is interpreted as code.

  - verdict: escalate
    reason: ...
    all:
      - { answer: screen.injection, field: noul, op: ">=", value: 0.7 }

field: noul | score | confidence | choice
op:    < <= > >= == !=
First matching rule wins; conditions are ANDed and short-circuit. One optional
`default: true` rule, last. Rubrics are validated at load, so a malformed rule fails
before any judgment runs. A rule whose answer is missing escalates, never falls through.

## Confidence

confidence = min over `deciding_answers` (the answers the matched rule read).
Answers a rule did not read never contribute. Noul has no confidence field, so
distance from 0.5 stands in for it. An automatic pass/fail below
confidence_floors[stakes] is downgraded to review.

## Exit codes

Verdicts:   0 pass, 1 fail, 2 review, 3 escalate, 4 skip
Operational: 10 error, 11 usage  (the judgment did not happen)

Operational codes sit outside the verdict range so a crash is never read as `fail`.
JSON on stdout, logs on stderr.
